links.comparator_used: Baseline LLM without the retrieved ophthalmic knowledge base (training knowledge alone); GPT-4 also benchmarked
links.outcome: Human ranking score and scientific consensus on 300 ophthalmology clinical questions
links.effect: Human ranking score 0.60 vs 0.48 baseline (difference 0.12; 95% CI, 0.02-0.22; P = .02); scientific consensus 84.0% vs 46.5% (difference 37.5%; 95% CI, 29.0%-46.0%; P < .001). Not different from GPT-4: 0.61 (P = .89) and 79.2% (P = .06).
links.quote: The retrieval-augmented LLM had a score of 0.60, a difference of 0.12 (95% CI, 0.02-0.22; P = .02) from baseline and not different from GPT-4 with a score of 0.61 (difference = 0.01; 95% CI, -0.11 to 0.13; P = .89).

design_hint: retrieval grounding with knowledge base added to baseline LLM
